text:
Alex: quick idea — introduce a "hotkey shepherd" layer to reduce eviction thrash for a small set of ultra-hot prefixes
Maria: shepherd? can you sketch the invariant you want to protect?
Alex: basically: when a prefix becomes super-hot we give it a lightweight lease-like token (shepherd token) that biases eviction and colocates reads to avoid scatter. token is ephemeral and has backoff on failures
Sam: sounds similar to a soft-pin but with metadata about active readers. what's the difference vs current lease flow?
Alex: two big diffs: 1) token is cooperative and cheap (no strong fencing), 2) tokens encode a "shepherd level" (0..3) that controls eviction grace and replication of cached slices
Kevin: main worry = correctness on read-after-write and stale tombstones. cooperative tokens won't prevent racey demote+write sequences
Maria: +1 to Kevin. need clear rules for when writes must invalidate/hard-evict vs when token can stay optimistic
Sam: proposal: token includes an epoch and a last-write-hash. readers check epoch; writers bump epoch and optionally emit an invalidate event to the side channel. cheap reads skip heavyweight RPC if epoch matches
Alex: sketch of config snippet I tried locally:
```
hotkey_shepherd:
  token_ttl_ms: 2500
  backoff_ms: 200
  levels:
    - name: warm
      grace_ms: 500
    - name: hot
      grace_ms: 2000
    - name: blazing
      grace_ms: 8000
```
Maria: ok but we need fallback: if a node holding cache collapses, other nodes must be able to safely serve without violating write ordering
Kevin: my take: treat shepherd token as optimization only. The canonical correctness path remains leases + tombstone propagation. tokens speed reads but must be invalidated on any write that could affect the keyspace segment
Sam: agree. Implementation idea: make the shepherd token store a cheap in-memory map with async durable tombstone hooks. Writers synchronously update the epoch in the coordination layer but don't block reads unless they see mismatch
Alex: telemetry questions: how do we know tokens help? propose metrics: token-hit-rate, token-invalidation-rate, post-invalidation-staleness-samples, evict-churn-per-hotkey
Maria: add quantiles for read-latency while token present vs absent. also track token-memory-overhead per-slab
Kevin: testing plan: 1) unit tests for epoch bump + read-after-write races, 2) small multi-node chaos test with node crash and write spike, 3) staged canary on low-traffic shard
Alex: canary params I propose: 0.5% of traffic, track <1% stale reads over 1s window, rollback if >5 errors or sustained lat/poly increase
ops-bot: scheduled canary: cluster=canary-3 window=2h start=2026-04-02T03:00Z
Sam: one more interface question — how do we expose token semantics to Dedicated/Private deployments? config-only? api toggle?
Maria: config toggle is fine but add a runtime gate in console and SDK flag. ops teams need visibility and a kill-switch
Alex: also thought about eviction interaction: when a token exists, eviction should prefer shedding non-shepherd slabs first and only reclaim shepherded slices when grace expired. we need a bounded grace to avoid memory leak
Kevin: add an eviction-credit debit: each token consumes X credits; eviction scheduler honors credit budget. that enforces boundedness and fairness
Sam: nice. credits -> fairshare also helps multi-tenant isolation. tie credits to tenant SLAs maybe
Maria: doc/ops checklist: - migration steps from current soft-pin -> shepherd tokens - telemetry dashboards - rollback playbook - canary checklist - KB entry for SRE on how to interpret token telemetry
Alex: i'll write an RFC draft with the state machine diagram (token lifecycle: allocate -> refresh -> epoch-mismatch -> invalidate -> expire) and a small reference impl in the prefix layer
Kevin: please include explicit invariants: "read sees write" and "tombstone visibility bound" with formal failure modes
Sam: i'll volunteer to pair on the chaos tests
Maria: tagging release:eng-runtime for visibility. also assign a short spike to measure token memory perf
Alex: thanks — i'll post the RFC link when ready. cc @Sam @Kevin @Maria :thumbsup:
Maria: :thumbsup:
Sam: happy to help on tests
Kevin: will sketch invariants tomorrow
ops-bot: reminder: RFC review sync scheduled 2026-04-05 17:00 UTC
